title: Virtual Networks and Subnets
description: Learn how Azure Virtual Networks isolate your cloud resources and how subnets segment traffic.

data.text: An Azure Virtual Network (VNet) is your own private network in the cloud. It is logically isolated from other customers and lets you control IP addressing, DNS, security, and routing.
Subnets divide a VNet into smaller network segments. You can use subnets to separate web servers from databases, or to apply different security rules.

data.title: VNet Properties
items: Address space — a private IP range like 10.0.0.0/16
Service endpoints — secure direct access to Azure services

data.title: Create a VNet with Subnets (Azure CLI)
data.content: Provision a VNet with separate subnets for web and database tiers.
data.code:
az network vnet create   --name myVNet   --resource-group myRG   --address-prefix 10.0.0.0/16   --subnet-name web-subnet   --subnet-prefix 10.0.1.0/24

az network vnet subnet create   --vnet-name myVNet   --resource-group myRG   --name db-subnet   --address-prefix 10.0.2.0/24

data.caption: A VNet containing a web subnet and a database subnet.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    VNet["VNet (10.0.0.0/16)"] --> WebSubnet["web-subnet (10.0.1.0/24)"]
    VNet --> DbSubnet["db-subnet (10.0.2.0/24)"]
    WebSubnet --> WebApp["App Service / VM"]
    DbSubnet --> Sql["Azure SQL / VM"]

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: VNets provide isolated private networking in Azure.
Subnets segment traffic and allow different security rules per segment.
Plan your address space carefully — overlapping ranges cannot peer.
data.takeaway: Every Azure application that needs private communication should start with a well-designed VNet.
